page: Amazon Web Services m8i.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose instance powered by Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this system provides 96 physical cores and 192 dedicated vCPUs clocked at 3.9 GHz. It features a 480 MB Level 3 cache, 2 MB Level 2 cache per core, and hardware acceleration extensions including Intel AMX and AVX-512. The instance includes 768 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. There is no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions, and no integrated GPU accelerators. Network connectivity is delivered through a high-throughput 75 Gbps baseline interface.

Benchmark results place the m8i.metal-48xl in the top tier for multi-threaded compute and data handling workloads. Multi-core performance across stress-ng and PassMark registers within the top decile, complemented by strong single-core scores. Memory subsystem performance is robust, producing 598.38 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 242.35 GB/sec in write operations. In practical application tests, the instance records 286.83 million Redis SET operations per second and 282.47 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Compute-intensive pipelines such as Clang software compilation and decompression also execute at top-tier speeds. While prompt processing for language models shows exceptional throughput, single-threaded text generation throughput remains closer to median expectations.

By delivering dedicated bare-metal access without hypervisor overhead, the m8i.metal-48xl offers strong resource efficiency for dense, highly concurrent environments. The absence of local NVMe storage requires architectural reliance on external network volumes, which introduces network I/O dependencies for disk-bound operations. However, the high compute density, 75 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and substantial memory capacity yield an efficient footprint for consolidating container fleets, running large-scale in-memory databases, hosting private virtualization environments, and processing intensive batch compilation or analytical workloads.

The system features 96 physical cores, 192 dedicated vCPUs operating at 3.9 GHz, and an expansive 480 MB L3 cache with Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions. Memory is configured at 768 GB, adhering to a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPUs, instead relying on external storage solutions paired with 75 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. In benchmarks, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded compute capabilities, exceeding 286 million Redis operations per second and showing high throughput in software compilation and uncached memory transfers. While disk-heavy setups depend entirely on network storage, the hardware configuration provides high resource density without virtualization overhead, making it well matched for enterprise container orchestration, in-memory databases, large-scale web services, and distributed compute workloads.
